task: cme-2025-2027: CME Group holiday schedules, calendar years 2025-2027, per product group
coverage:
CME Group holiday schedules for calendar years 2025, 2026 and 2027, per product group, from CME's own trading-hours channel. Evidence bytes, an INDEX.md with sha256 for every artifact, and the derived working files are under /Users/agedvagabond/Developer/exchange-hours-research/holidays/raw/cme-2025-2027/. Work done 2026-09-12 UTC.

ROUND 1 FIX (2026-09-12 UTC). This payload supersedes cme-2025-2027.r0.json, which is kept beside it; the round-0 bytes hash sha256 4cd4706a8e989cd0d59abe1279e4a03f3aee9b0b80c99476d2fe49466584bd50. New evidence retrieved in this round is under raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/ with its own INDEX.md. Seven things changed, each re-read from the saved bytes rather than taken on anyone's word:
(1) THANKSGIVING 2025 RE-SOURCED. The round-0 claim that no capture of the 2025 windows later than 2024-12-20 exists is false for Thanksgiving. A fresh CDX run finds 45 captures of fromEventDate=2025-11-26&toEventDate=2025-11-28, 44 of them from the 2026-01-29 crawl, i.e. two months AFTER the holiday. The latest, 2026-01-29T01:23:09Z, was retrieved and is now D09; the 2024-12-20 publication is kept as D09P and is explicitly marked superseded. The two agree on every instant; they differ on eight product-dates, all on Friday 2025-11-28, where the finalised publication additionally prints a morning pre-open/open pair. The 2025-11-28 verbatim lines are re-quoted from D09.
(2) 2025-07-03 EQUITY INDEX. ES closes 12:15 CT on Thursday 2025-07-03 in D07 while ZN, 6E, CL, GC and BTC all close 16:00 CT that day - an early final close at a stated instant, identical in shape to 2025-11-28. It was carried as status 'modified' with no close_instant; it is now early_close with close_instant 12:15 CT. This is the only Independence-Day-eve equity-index early close in the 2025 set.
(3) STATUS VOCABULARY MADE SELF-CONSISTENT. The 17 rows noted [N3] - FX, and Cryptocurrency before it went 24/7, on Monday and Thursday holidays - were labelled 'normal' although they differ from CME's normal grid twice over: no 16:00 CT final close on the date, and the pre-open at 16:00 rather than 16:45, so the holiday carries no trade date of its own and the whole span rolls into the next business day. The converse single deviation ([N6], final close present but no evening re-open) was already 'modified'. The [N3] rows are now 'modified' too.
(4) 2027-12-23 CRYPTOCURRENCY. Its event TIMES equal the normal Thursday grid, but the 16:01/16:02 re-open carries trade date 2027-12-27, skipping the closed Friday 2027-12-24 - on a normal Thursday it would carry the next calendar day (checked against the reference week, where only the Friday row rolls to Monday). Status 'normal' [N8] becomes 'modified' [N18].
(5) N17 DEFINED, N18 ADDED. N17 was used on three rows and never defined. N17 = no day session on the holiday; only a 16:00 CT pre-open and a 17:00 CT open, both already carrying the next business day's trade date (verified against D01: on 2025-01-01 ES, ZN, CL, 6E, GC, BTC and CSC each publish exactly '16:00 preopen /TD 2025-01-02; 17:00 open /TD 2025-01-02', while ZC, LE and LBR publish nothing). N18 is defined in (4).
(6) RE-FETCH PATH REPAIRED. The archived URLs in raw/cme-2025-2027/INDEX.md omit the '&isProtected&_t=<epoch>' suffix that is part of the archived URL, so following one literally returns a Wayback 404. raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/REFETCH.tsv now lists, for all 25 archived service artifacts, the exact one-step id_ replay URL, rebuilt from the fresh CDX rather than from the old working file. raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/MANIFEST-cme-2025-2027.sha256 additionally hashes all 180 files on disk under raw/cme-2025-2027/, not just the 72 load-bearing artifacts INDEX.md lists.
(7) THE UNCHECKED SATURDAY RECORDED. CME's own 2025 Globex table states the Thanksgiving period as '27 - 29 November 2025', but no archived call of the service covers Saturday 2025-11-29. That gap is now an explicit missing[] entry, with the 2026 and 2027 equivalents queried live (D52, D53) as mitigation.
Everything the verification did not dispute is unchanged: no other instant, verbatim, document id, tier or status was touched.

STATUS VOCABULARY, as used below. 'closed' - the family publishes no tradeable session on the date. 'early_close' - a session runs and ends earlier than the family's normal grid for that weekday, and close_instant carries the stated instant. 'modified' - the published event list differs from the normal grid in some way other than an earlier final close (a missing evening leg, a missing final close, a pre-open at a different time, a trade date that rolls past the holiday). 'normal' - the published event list and its trade dates equal the family's normal grid for that weekday. 'unknown' - only a publication known to be superseded survives for the date, and it is not carried.

SOURCE. cmegroup.com refuses this machine directly (HTTP 403, 'This IP address is blocked due to suspected web scraping activity'), so live pages and service calls were read through the public reader https://r.jina.ai/<url> and history through the Wayback Machine with id_ replay. CME no longer publishes a per-holiday hours PDF or XLS: from the 2025 calendar year the holiday hours ARE the interactive table on https://www.cmegroup.com/trading-hours.html ('Please note that with the 2025 calendar year the CME Group will be providing downloadable holiday calendars for Globex and incorporating with Regular Trading hours into one location'), and every 'Holiday Schedule' link on the Holiday Calendar page points at that page. The per-holiday PDFs that do exist for 2025/2026 ('...-holiday-settlement-times-<year>.pdf', '<year>-...-clearing-advisory.pdf', 'otc-...pdf') carry settlement-price and clearing-cycle information only and state no trading hours; the MLK-2025 clearing advisory routes trading hours back to 'CME Group Holiday Calendar / CME Group Trading Hours'. Those two were retrieved and indexed to document that the channel was read and is not a session source (LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY).

CHANNEL AND TIER. The rows below come from https://www.cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours-by-product?...&fromEventDate=&toEventDate= - the endpoint the trading-hours page itself calls to render its per-asset-class Holiday Hours table. That is the operator's own trading-hours service, so T2 under LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES, not T1. It was validated against the T1 rendering: for Thanksgiving 2026 the page prints rows labelled Interest Rates / Equities / Energy / Grains / FX / Metals / Livestock / Dairy / Cryptocurrencies / Lumber and each printed row matches the service rows for ZN / ES / CL / ZC / 6E / GC / LE / CSC / BTC / LBR event for event (e.g. printed 'Friday 27 Nov 2026 | Interest Rates | TRADE DATE: Fri 27 Nov 12:15 closed' = service ZN eventDate 2026-11-27 12:15 closed, trade date 2026-11-27). The saved rendering is live/trading-hours-live.md.

ZONE. Verbatim from the page: 'Trading hours are subject to change and are in U.S. Central Time unless otherwise stated.' Every instant recorded below is therefore CT as printed; CME prints no ET column in this channel, so no ET value is asserted. The page's free-text Holiday Notes do print CT/ET pairs, but only for TAS/TAM trade-type variants (e.g. 'Gold TAS: Early close 11:30 CT / 12:30 ET'), which are not the family sessions.

EVENT VOCABULARY, verbatim from the same page: PREOPEN 'Order Entry, modification, and cancel are allowed. No order matching.'; OPEN 'Start of continuous trading phase. Order matching begins.'; Paused 'Interruption of continuous trading. Only order cancellation is allowed. No order matching.'; pcp (POST CLOSE - PREOPEN) 'Allows GTC/GTD orders only placement, modification, and cancellation. No order matching.'; closed 'Final Close of the date. Day and GTD (current trade date) orders are eliminated.' This distinction matters: on the Monday holidays CME does NOT publish a 'closed' event at noon - it publishes a preopen, i.e. matching stops but the trade date does not end and the whole Sunday-evening-through-Monday span carries the following business day's trade date. Those rows are marked early_close with the instant, and the note says the event type is preopen.

ENUMERATION. Archive CDX was run first over cmegroup.com/tools-information/holiday-calendar*, cmegroup.com/trading-hours* and cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours* (results saved under cdx/). The live service carries only FORWARD holidays - as of 2026-09-12 it starts at Labor Day 2026-09-07 and runs to New Year 2028-01-01 - so 2025 and 2026-Jan..Jul holidays were taken from Wayback captures of the same endpoint, and 2026-09 onward from live retrieval. Where more than one capture of a window exists the most recent was used; the fresh CDX run of 2026-09-12 re-checked this window by window and the one window where it did not hold - Thanksgiving 2025 - was re-sourced (see D09/D09P below). CME's own forward holiday list (services/trading-hours-filters, saved as api/filters.json) supplied the holiday dates and each holiday's start/end period for 2026-09-07 through 2028-01-01.

BASELINE. 'Status' is stated against CME's own non-holiday grid, taken from a clean reference week 2026-10-18..2026-10-24 pulled from the same service (live/normal/*.json), not from any pattern assumed by me. Each family row's verbatim carries the published event list AND that normal grid so the comparison is re-checkable. The per-date, per-product rows with baselines and deviation flags are in raw/cme-2025-2027/FINAL_ROWS.json; a readable review is FINAL_REVIEW.txt.

GROUPS. The ten groups CME prints map to these products, which are exactly the ten the trading-hours page itself queries: Equity Index=ES (E-mini S&P 500), Interest Rates=ZN (10-Year T-Note), FX=6E (Euro FX), Energy=CL (Crude Oil), Metals=GC (Gold), Grains & Oilseeds=ZC (Corn), Livestock=LE (Live Cattle), Cryptocurrency=BTC (Bitcoin), Dairy=CSC (Cash-Settled Cheese), Lumber=LBR (Lumber). From Labor Day 2026 forward the Nikkei-specific line (NKD Nikkei/USD, NIY Nikkei/JPY), soybeans (ZS), wheat (ZW), lean hogs (HE) and Class III milk (DC) were pulled as a second id set; where they appear they track ES (Nikkei), ZC (ZS/ZW), LE (HE) and CSC (DC) exactly.

STRUCTURE OF THE ROWS. One holidays[] entry per CME holiday. Inside it, families[] carries one row per (product group set, date): the holiday's own date is given for every group including the ones that ran normally, and the adjacent dates in CME's own window (eve, day after, the Sunday evening leg, and the Saturday sessions) are given only where CME publishes something other than the normal grid. Groups that share an identical published event list on a date are listed together in one row. 'family' ends with '| date YYYY-MM-DD' naming the date the row governs. Note codes N1..N18 and EC are expanded in raw/cme-2025-2027/INDEX.md (N17 and N18 are defined in raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/INDEX.md and appended to the original INDEX.md): N17 = no day session on the holiday; only a 16:00 CT pre-open and a 17:00 CT open, both already carrying the next business day's trade date. N18 = the published event TIMES equal the family's normal grid for that weekday, but the re-open carries a trade date that skips the following closed holiday, so the date does carry a holiday trade-date roll.

WHAT THE DATA SHOWS, in outline. Monday/Thursday-Friday holidays (MLK, Presidents', Memorial, Labor, Juneteenth 2025, Thanksgiving) halt Equity Index and Interest Rates at 12:00 CT and Energy and Metals at 13:30 CT with a 17:00 CT reopen; FX and (pre-24/7) Cryptocurrency keep the ordinary 16:00-17:00 CT pause; Grains & Oilseeds have no day session and open 19:00 CT for the next trade date; Livestock, Lumber and (on some) Dairy do not trade at all. Good Friday 2025 and 2027 are a full Globex closure for every family (crypto excepted in 2027, which is 24/7 from 2026-05-29 and trades through). Good Friday 2026 is the exception CME itself flags, verbatim from the T1 operator page D50 (line 2498 of html/trading-hours-20250830.html): 'Due to the US Employment Situation Release on April 3, 2026, CME Group Equities, FX, Cryptocurrency and Interest Rate products will have unique Closes and Settlements for trade date April 3rd.' The same list continues, still D50: 'All other CME, CBT, NYMEX and COMEX products will have their settlements copied from April 2nd to April 3rd.' and 'No trading for Friday April 3th  trade date in observence of Good Friday.' (sic). D50 is T1 corroboration that Equities, FX, Cryptocurrency and Interest Rates traded that day and everything else did not, but it states no instants; the instants - Equities close 08:15 CT, Interest Rates, FX and Cryptocurrency 10:15 CT - come only from the T2 service document D14, which is what those rows cite. Independence Day (2025-07-04, 2026-07-03, 2027-07-05) and Juneteenth 2026/2027 run a 12:00 CT final close for the 24-hour groups with Grains, Livestock, Lumber and Dairy shut. The day after Thanksgiving is an early close at 12:15 CT (Equity Index, Interest Rates, Nikkei), 13:45 CT (FX, Energy, Metals, pre-24/7 Crypto) and 12:05 CT (Grains, Livestock, Lumber), with Dairy shut. Christmas Eve is 12:15 CT (Equity Index, Interest Rates, Nikkei), 12:45 CT (FX, Energy, Metals), 12:05 CT (Grains, Livestock, Lumber) and 12:00 CT (Dairy); Christmas Day and New Year's Day are full closures. New Year's Eve and the Thursday before Good Friday are a normal 16:00 CT final close with no evening reopen.

TWO THINGS WORTH FLAGGING TO THE CRATE. (1) After the Friday holidays of 2026 and 2027 CME publishes a SATURDAY session for the 24-hour groups - 2026-06-20, 2026-07-04 and 2027-06-19 all carry 'open 05:00 CT / closed 17:00 CT' with the following Monday's trade date, against a normally empty Saturday. These are in the rows as status modified, note N11. Saturday 2026-04-04 after Good Friday 2026 does NOT carry one (checked against the service for window 2026-04-02..04). (2) From 2026-05-29 Cryptocurrency is 24/7: on holidays it publishes only '16:01 preopen / 16:02 open' (the 16:00 CT final close is omitted because there is no settlement) and on full closure days such as Christmas 2026, New Year 2027, Good Friday 2027, Juneteenth 2027 and Christmas 2027 it does not appear as a deviation at all - it trades straight through with the trade date rolling.

NOT CME GLOBEX HOLIDAYS. Columbus Day and Veterans Day appear nowhere in CME's Globex holiday list (api/filters.json) even though CME publishes clearing advisories, settlement-times PDFs and OTC notices for them; Globex trades a normal session on both. They are therefore not recorded as holidays here.

RESIDUAL RISK. Eight 2025 windows - New Year (2024-12-31..2025-01-02), MLK, Presidents' Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day and Labor Day - rest on the single Wayback capture 2024-12-20T15:53:40Z of the service, and CME states on the same page 'This schedule is subject to change. Trading hours are usually finalized approximately two weeks prior to the holiday.' A fresh CDX enumeration of cmegroup.com/services/trading-hours-by-product* (raw/cme-2025-2027-fix/cdx/cdx_thbp_all_fix.json, 688 rows, retrieved 2026-09-12) confirms each of those eight windows has no capture later than 2024-12-20 (the New Year window has a second, earlier capture at 2024-07-08T16:14:39Z), so those rows are CME's published future as of 2024-12-20 rather than a post-finalisation statement. They are internally consistent with the 2026 and 2027 rows for the same holidays, which are sourced from later captures and from live retrieval. The three remaining 2025/26 windows DO have post-holiday captures and are sourced from them: Thanksgiving 2025 (45 captures, latest 2026-01-29T01:23:09Z = D09), Christmas 2025 (45 captures, latest 2026-01-29T01:23:09Z, content-identical to the 2026-01-29T01:21:59Z bytes already saved as D10 - re-fetched and compared in this round) and New Year 2026 (51 captures, latest 2026-07-22T11:42:22Z, content-identical schedule for schedule to D11's 2026-06-19T11:41:05Z bytes - re-fetched and compared in this round).
